title: Why is Everything Boring Now

notes.note: Dookie was released in February 1994. Sum 41 formed in 1996 and had its mainstream breakthrough with 'Fat Lip' and All Killer No Filler in 2001 — about 7 years after Dookie, not 3.
notes.claim: Sum 41 emerged approximately 3 years after Green Day's Dookie.
notes.context_paragraph: And then Dookie came out and Green Day found that perfect balance of having the edge still but being very mass appeal. And within what? 3 years? Sum 41? You know? I'm not critiquing Sum 41 in particular, but but that kind of punk became like so mass appeal and so clean

sources.quote: Dookie is the third studio album and major-label debut by the American rock band Green Day, released on February 1, 1994
sources.explanation: Confirms the release date of Dookie.

sources.quote: All Killer No Filler is the debut studio album[A] by Canadian rock band Sum 41, released on May 8, 2001.
sources.explanation: Confirms the release date of the breakthrough album.

sources.quote: The album was a big commercial success; it was certified platinum by the Recording Industry Association of America in August 2001
sources.explanation: Supports the claim that this album was the band's mainstream breakthrough.
Confirms the release date of the single 'Fat Lip'.

sources.quote: It is the band's most successful single to date, topping the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart.
sources.explanation: Supports that 'Fat Lip' was the band's mainstream breakthrough single.
